title: [Chapitre] I. Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques) : notes manuscrites (05/06/1986).

errors: NB2 ('at most two segments with the same extremities, two iff circle component') is not true for general graphs without further axioms. A theta graph, or any multigraph with k parallel edges between two branch points x and y, gives k segments with δI = {x,y}. The claim needs extra hypotheses, e.g. that adjacency or segments are minimal and that extremities of parallel segments are non-critical, or that branching is encoded through distinct places. Grothendieck flags it only as a presumption ('Je présume').

E1 as written ('non-disjoint' is an equivalence relation) needs transitivity justified: overlapping is not transitive for general regions. It works only if places are point-like (germs or branches at a point), which seems to be the intended meaning.

ideas.what: Recursive (on dimension n) combinatorial axiomatization of 'forms', i.e. tame topological spaces, starting from discrete sets of places in dimension 0
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial models of stratified / tame spaces; regular CW or graph models; o-minimal cell decompositions
ideas.usually_credited_to: tame topology program: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984); o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight; stratified spaces: Whitney, Thom, Mather
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 (topologie modérée) states the general aim; this specific axiomatics appears unpublished

ideas.what: Places distinct from points: several critical places can define the same critical point; points are the quotient of places by the non-disjointness relation
ideas.modern_name: branches / places over a singular point (as in normalization of curves); exit paths / local branches in stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Dedekind–Weber places; normalization); exit-path view: MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie

ideas.what: Redundancy of the adjacency relation: adjacency is defined by the existence of a segment with those extremities
Specialization relation from critical to non-critical places
ideas.modern_name: specialization order of a finite (Alexandrov) topological space / face poset of a stratification

missed.claim: A combinatorial, place-based (rather than point-based) axiomatics of 1-dimensional tame forms, intended to be iterated over the dimension n. It is an early, concrete attempt at the 'topologie modérée' foundations announced in the Esquisse. The page does not get beyond tentative data and a first axiom.
missed.quote: Approche vers une construction récurrente (sur l'entier naturel n) d'une 'géométrie des formes de dimension n'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest as evidence of how Grothendieck concretely approached tame topology in 1986. Mathematically it is subsumed by graph theory, o-minimal cell decomposition and exit-path or stratified-space formalisms, so it offers little that is new.

deep.surprise_reason: A tentative, partly incorrect first draft of an axiomatics for 1-dimensional 'forms' (essentially graphs with branch places). It is interesting archivally as a concrete trace of the tame-topology program, but contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: likely 'appelés "les extrémités" du segment' rather than 'l'une extrémités'.
(8): likely '(l'ensemble des lieux dits "sur le segment")'. The '𝒳' / 'l'un des lieux' reading is doubtful.
NB2: '(vrai [?] d'un) cercle' is probably '(modèle d'un) cercle'.
E1: probably 'la relation "x et y ne sont pas disjoints" est une relation d'équivalence'.
The following lines likely say that the quotient (equivalence classes) defines the points of the form, critical classes giving critical or branching points.
